: Note: [We will meet ***weekly on Tuesdays, 2:00--4:00PM***, almost always in
2-426 (except for on 22^nd^ September).]{.underline}

Our theme thie term is *foundations of causal machine learning*, cutting across
modern frameworks from targeted learning [@vdl2006targeted; @gruber2010bounded;
@vdl2011targeted] to construct asymptotically linear estimators of pathwise
differentiable statistical parameters to Neyman orthogonality and double
machine learning [@chernozhukov2018double; @foster2023orthogonal]. To deepen
our perspective, we will also consider common areas of study between these,
including doubly robust inference [@benkeser2017doubly], the relationship
between pathwise differentiability and Neyman orthognality
[@chen2026equivalence], and recent advances in the estimation of nuisance
functions [@mccartan2026gaussian]. As with [Spring
2026](archive/spring2026.qmd), we alternate weekly between presentations of the
assigned readings and informal research-connection talks covering the
relationship between recently discussed topics and ongoing projects in our
group.

Time permitting, we may discuss additional topics---listed below---which may
replace readings in the above list (pending group discussion) or otherwise
serve as potential readings for Spring 2027.

- **Classics in semi-parametric theory**: @klaassen1987consistent,
  @robins1995semiparametric
- **Inference in time-varying, longitudinal settings**: @westling2020causal,
  @diaz2021nonparametric, @luedtke2018sequential, @diaz2024causal,
  @diaz2026modified, @murphy2003optimal, @rotnitzky2017multiply
* **Function estimation, adaptive inference, and frontier topics**:
  @kennedy2023towards, @chernozhukov2024conditional
  @lan2024causal, @vanderlaan2025automatic, @luedtke2024onestep,
  @liu2017semiparametric, @liu2020nearly
